comments: The media-licensing operator (fictional; smp-) — photo and video licensing library. Everything below is the portal export
the studio took in 2022 and has hand-edited since; it is the record of the library estate.
Single resource group smp-rg. Deploy with scripts/deploy.sh.
NAME SUFFIX: storage accounts and the data factory are global DNS names, so every one of them
carries the nameSuffix parameter. scripts/deploy.sh derives that value from the subscription and
the resource group and passes the SAME value to the delivery templates under terraform/, which is
how both trees end up naming the same delivery account. Change it in one place only.
ORDERING: scripts/deploy.sh runs the terraform/ tree first and this template second, so where the
two describe the same property of smpdelivery<suffix> the value in this file is the one that

metadata.description: Region for every resource. Taken from the resource group, which scripts/deploy.sh creates from AZURE_LOCATION.
YYYY-MM-DD written to the AutoTeardown tag on every taggable resource. Supplied by deploy.sh from ~/.azure/journeys.env.

Lowercase alphanumeric suffix appended to every globally-unique name (three storage accounts and the data factory). No default: scripts/deploy.sh derives it from the subscription id and the resource group name and passes the same value to the terraform/ tree, so the two trees agree on what the delivery account is called. Storage account names are 3-24 lowercase alphanumerics with no hyphens; the longest stem here is 'smpdelivery' (11), which caps the suffix at 12.

Retention interval for the masters container. One day is the shortest Azure accepts. The studio's counsel asked for 7 years; the value here is what the studio actually set while it was still evaluating the feature.
Provisioned size of the wip-edit premium share, in GiB. 100 is the smallest a premium file share can be provisioned at, and premium shares bill on provisioned size rather than used size.

resources.comments: The library. RA-GRS: the studio pays for the read-only secondary because a licensing customer in another region reads catalogue thumbnails straight off the secondary endpoint, and because the 2024 insurance review asked for an off-region copy of the masters. minimumTlsVersion is set EXPLICITLY to TLS1_2 — ARM, CLI and PowerShell all leave the property unset by default, and an account with it unset permits TLS 1.0 and later.
resources.name: [variables('mediaAccountName')]

resources.comments: Camera-original stills and video, one folder per shoot. Read by the licensing site and by nothing else.
resources.name: [concat(variables('mediaAccountName'), '/default/', variables('mastersContainerName'))]

resources.comments: Watermarked web-resolution renders of everything in masters. Regenerated on demand, so they are treated as disposable.
resources.name: [concat(variables('mediaAccountName'), '/default/', variables('proxiesContainerName'))]

resources.comments: Landing area the photographers' uploader writes to. Emptied nightly by the copy the studio manager runs out of the data factory.
resources.name: [concat(variables('mediaAccountName'), '/default/', variables('intakeContainerName'))]

resources.comments: Write-once retention on the masters container, added in 2025 after the studio lost a shoot to an overwrite. The policy resource has only ever been PUT, never locked, so it stays in the Unlocked state: it still blocks overwrites and deletes of blobs inside the retention window, but the policy itself can be shortened, extended or removed. Locking it is a separate operation and is what makes it SEC 17a-4(f) compliant.
resources.name: [concat(variables('mediaAccountName'), '/default/', variables('mastersContainerName'), '/default')]

resources.comments: Proxy jobs. A blob landing under the intake container becomes a message here; the proxy generator on the office NAS drains it.
resources.name: [concat(variables('mediaAccountName'), '/default/', variables('proxyQueueName'))]

resources.comments: Tiering for the library. Rules are evaluated once a day and act on blobs whose last-modified time is older than the threshold; a blob that no rule prefix matches is left where it is. All three rules were written against the container layout of the day they were added.
resources.name: [concat(variables('mediaAccountName'), '/default')]

resources.comments: Scratch space for the edit bay. Premium file shares live on their own FileStorage account — the kind cannot be mixed with blob containers, and premium is LRS or ZRS only, so this account is not geo-replicated the way the library account is. accessTier is not a property of a FileStorage account; premium is the tier.
resources.name: [variables('wipAccountName')]

resources.comments: The share the two edit workstations map as W:. Premium shares bill on provisioned size, not on what is in them.
resources.name: [concat(variables('wipAccountName'), '/default/', variables('wipShareName'))]

resources.comments: Stood up in 2024 to give the edit bay a local cache of the W: share over its slow line. The service and its group exist; registering the edit-bay NAS needs the agent installed on the box itself, which is still on the studio manager's list.
resources.name: [variables('syncServiceName')]

resources.comments: The topology that would pair the edit-bay NAS with the wip-edit share. No server has been registered against it.
resources.name: [concat(variables('syncServiceName'), '/', variables('syncGroupName'))]

resources.comments: The factory the intake-to-masters move runs in. Its pipelines and linked services are authored in the ADF studio by the studio manager and live in the service, not in this file — the 2022 portal export captured the factory and nothing inside it, and nobody has exported it since.
resources.name: [variables('dataFactoryName')]

resources.comments: Blob events for the library account. A system topic is the storage account's own event source; it needs no endpoint validation handshake when it delivers to a storage queue in the same account.
resources.name: [variables('systemTopicName')]

resources.comments: Anything landing in intake becomes a proxy job. The generator is a scheduled task on the edit-bay NAS that drains proxy-jobs, renders the watermarked web copy and writes it to the proxies container.
resources.name: [concat(variables('systemTopicName'), '/', variables('proxySubscriptionName'))]

resources.comments: Public delivery origin for the licensing site's preview renders. Added to this file in 2025 so the estate export would list it — the edge contractor builds and owns it out of terraform/, and the containers on it are hers. accessTier Hot is what the studio wants: previews are served on every catalogue page view and a cool read is billed per gigabyte.
resources.name: [variables('deliveryAccountName')]
